sections.heading: How Commview Thinks About AI in Business
intro: AI is not a strategy in itself. It is another way to change how work gets done.

That means we do not start with a model, platform or list of fashionable use cases. We start with the operation. Where is time being lost? Which work repeats? Where are people moving information between systems? Where does slow access to information hold up a decision?
If AI can materially improve the way that work happens, it has a job to do. If a simpler process change, automation or existing tool solves the problem better, we use that instead.
The point is not to add more AI. The point is to make the business work better.

heading: Automate the work.
Not the accountability.
sections.body: AI can draft, classify, summarise and make recommendations. It cannot take responsibility for the decision. The humans who understand your customers, your business and the consequences still need to make the call. We help you design AI solutions that support better decisions, not replace them.

items.a: AI consulting helps a business identify where artificial intelligence can create useful operational or commercial change, then plan and implement it. For Commview, that starts with the work rather than the technology. We examine the workflow, the problem, the available data and the consequence of errors before deciding whether AI belongs in the solution.

items.q: How much does AI consulting cost?
items.a: AI consulting costs depend on the scope of the problem, the systems involved and whether the work covers diagnosis, implementation or a broader operating change. Commview does not publish a fixed price because a focused workflow project and a cross-functional transformation are materially different engagements. We scope the work around the outcome required.

items.q: What is the difference between AI consulting and an AI agency?
items.a: The labels overlap, so the practical difference is usually the work being bought. An AI agency may focus on building a particular automation, agent or technical solution. AI consulting can start earlier by deciding where AI is worth using, redesigning the workflow and connecting implementation to the wider operating and commercial context.

items.q: Can AI actually reduce our costs?
items.a: AI can reduce costs when it removes enough repetitive work, delay or manual processing to justify the implementation and ongoing operating cost. It does not automatically make a process cheaper. The business case should compare the current workflow with the proposed one and measure what changes after deployment.

items.q: Do we need an AI strategy before we start?
items.a: Not always. A B2B scale-up can often start with a specific operational problem, test a useful intervention and learn from it before creating a wider AI programme. A broader strategy becomes more valuable when multiple teams, systems, governance requirements and investment decisions need to be coordinated.

items.q: How do you decide which AI use case to tackle first?
items.a: Start with the work that creates meaningful friction and can be measured. We look at frequency, time consumed, process complexity, available information, error consequences and the value of improving the workflow. The first use case should be useful enough to matter but contained enough to test without creating unnecessary transformation risk.

sections.heading: Find the work where AI can actually earn its place.
